fragen.bildwunsch: A chrome humanoid head in three-quarter view, one eye socket glowing red, half sunk in shadow, shot like a news still
fragen.frage: Let us start simply. What is artificial intelligence?
antworten: An umbrella term for methods that have changed completely over seventy years
Software that thinks the way a human does
A machine that is aware of itself
The technology behind ChatGPT
fragen.erklaerung: What counts as AI keeps moving. Chess programs and spell checkers were AI once and are software now. Awareness is not part of any definition anybody works with, and ChatGPT is one product in a seventy-year-old field.

schlagzeilen.2: Researcher at TU Vienna: the machines are awake
schlagzeilen.3: TU researcher: artificial intelligence is ChatGPT

fragen.bildwunsch: A human hand and a chrome robotic hand reaching for the same red button on a console
fragen.frage: What is the difference between machine learning and artificial intelligence?
antworten: Machine learning is one method inside the wider field of AI
They are two words for the same thing
Machine learning is the newer and more powerful one
AI needs rules, machine learning needs none
fragen.erklaerung: AI is the field, machine learning is the method that currently dominates it. Rule-based systems are AI too and learn nothing, which is why the last answer gets it backwards.

schlagzeilen.1: Researcher: AI and machine learning are the same
schlagzeilen.2: TU researcher: machine learning has overtaken AI
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher: real AI runs without any rules

fragen.bildwunsch: A gallery wall of identical portraits, one of them melting into coloured noise
fragen.frage: And what is generative AI, then?
antworten: Models that produce new examples by drawing from a learned distribution
Models that work without training data
A technique that has existed since ChatGPT
Software that is creative
fragen.erklaerung: Producing instead of predicting, that is the whole difference. They need training data very much indeed, diffusion models go back to 2015, and creativity is a word nobody in the field can define well enough to defend on television.

schlagzeilen.1: TU researcher: new AI needs no data
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher at TU Vienna calls machines creative

fragen.bildwunsch: A mushroom cloud on the horizon seen through the window of an empty control room, monitors glowing
fragen.frage: Straight out: will a language model kill us all?
antworten: Nobody knows, and the field is genuinely split on it
No, that is science fiction
Yes, without strict regulation it is likely
Researchers agree the risk is small
fragen.erklaerung: The split is not slight: a survey of AI researchers produced a median of five percent for extinction risk, while attendees of a 2026 Harvard event gave a median of fifty. Andrew Ng calls the worry science fiction; people of equal standing call it the question of the century. Any of the other three presents a position as a finding.

schlagzeilen.1: TU researcher laughs off extinction risk
schlagzeilen.2: TU researcher: AI will kill us

fragen.bildwunsch: A charred briefcase open on a street, emergency lights flashing blue across the wet asphalt
fragen.frage: You have an image generated and it shows a bomb. Who is liable?
antworten: Whoever publishes or uses it, and depending on the case the operator too
Nobody, because no human drew it
The provider of the model, always
The person who wrote the prompt, in every case
fragen.erklaerung: Liability attaches to the person who acts, so to publishing and using. The provider can be liable as well, but not automatically, and writing a prompt you never act on is not an act. A tool does not absorb responsibility, and neither does a circular saw.

schlagzeilen.1: TU researcher: nobody liable for AI bombs
schlagzeilen.2: Researcher blames AI firms for everything
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher: typing a prompt makes you liable

fragen.bildwunsch: A gavel coming down on a stack of printed artworks, one sheet flying off the pile
fragen.frage: Who owns an image that an AI produced?
antworten: In Germany and Austria no copyright arises unless a human shaped it
Whoever wrote the prompt
The company that trained the model
Nobody, so you may do whatever you like with it
fragen.erklaerung: The prompt alone is not enough; both the Munich district court and the Düsseldorf higher regional court took that view in 2026. What you rework by hand can be protected. And no copyright arising does not mean you may do as you like: that is governed by your contract with the provider.

schlagzeilen.1: Prompt makes you the artist, says TU
schlagzeilen.2: Researcher: AI images belong to the corporations
schlagzeilen.3: TU researcher declares AI images free for all

fragen.bildwunsch: A face on a screen splitting in two halves, one photographic and one visibly synthetic
fragen.frage: Does AI-made content have to be labelled?
antworten: Yes, Article 50 of the AI Act has applied since 2 August 2026
No, that is voluntary
Only for text, not for images
Yes, and retroactively for everything ever made
fragen.erklaerung: Up to fifteen million euros or three percent of global turnover, and it catches practically anyone running a chatbot or using AI images in marketing. It covers image, audio, video and text alike, and it does not apply retroactively.

schlagzeilen.2: TU researcher: AI pictures need no label
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher demands labels on all old content

fragen.bildwunsch: A humanoid robot seated in an armchair reading a book, lamp light on its blank face
fragen.frage: Does the system actually understand what it says?
antworten: It estimates the likely continuation; whether that is understanding is unsettled
Yes, it has a model of the world
No, it only shuffles words around
Yes, at this size it must
fragen.erklaerung: The mechanism is uncontested. What understanding means is not, and saying yes or no on television sells a philosophical position as a finding. The brisk no is a claim too, merely one that sounds cleverer.

schlagzeilen.1: TU researcher: the machine understands us
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher at TU Vienna: size makes machines understand

fragen.bildwunsch: A library reading room where the books dissolve into blank pages towards the back wall
fragen.frage: Then why does it invent sources?
antworten: Because it produces the likely continuation, and likely is not true
Because the training data was faulty
It is a bug that will be fixed shortly
Because it wants to please the user
fragen.erklaerung: Not a defect but the very property that makes the thing useful. An invented source is produced exactly the way a correct one is. Anyone claiming it will shortly be fixed is selling something, and the machine wants nothing at all.

schlagzeilen.1: Researcher blames the data for AI lies
schlagzeilen.2: TU promises end of AI hallucinations
schlagzeilen.3: TU researcher: the machine wants to please us

fragen.bildwunsch: A queue of people with cardboard boxes outside a glass office tower at dusk
fragen.frage: Is this going to cost us our jobs?
antworten: The studies contradict each other; the figures are forecasts, not measurements
Yes, office work above all
No, more jobs appear than disappear
Only for people who refuse to learn it
fragen.erklaerung: Everyone wants a number and none is defensible. What you can say: tasks are measurably shifting, employment is not, and any forecast beyond 2030 is an opinion with a decimal point. The fourth answer is a threat dressed as advice.

schlagzeilen.1: TU researcher predicts office job wipeout
schlagzeilen.2: Researcher: AI creates more jobs than it kills
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher warns: learn AI or lose your job

fragen.bildwunsch: Cooling towers at night against a black sky, steam lit from below, power lines in front
fragen.frage: How much electricity does all this consume?
antworten: Data centres are at about 1.5 percent of world electricity, and AI is part of that
AI already uses more than aviation
It is negligible compared to industry
AI will consume a quarter of world electricity by 2030
fragen.erklaerung: About 415 terawatt hours a year, a good 1.5 percent, with 945 expected by 2030. Streaming and cloud are the larger part of that; AI is a share of it. Neither the dismissal nor the quarter survives contact with the IEA figures.

schlagzeilen.1: TU: AI burns more power than flying
schlagzeilen.2: Researcher waves away AI power use
schlagzeilen.3: TU researcher: AI to eat a quarter of world power

fragen.bildwunsch: A courtroom of the European Union, twelve gold stars on the wall, one empty defendant's box
fragen.frage: When does this AI law actually apply?
antworten: In stages: prohibitions since 2025, transparency since August 2026, high risk from 2027
All of it from 2 August 2026
It has been postponed altogether
Not before 2030
fragen.erklaerung: Staggered, and the postponement is recent: the Digital Omnibus moved the high-risk duties to December 2027, and to August 2028 for Annex I systems. Anyone reading slides made before May 2026 is quoting the wrong dates.

schlagzeilen.1: Researcher: AI law fully in force
schlagzeilen.2: TU researcher: the AI law is off the table

fragen.bildwunsch: A shredder overflowing with exam papers, one sheet caught halfway in
fragen.frage: You are at a university. May you put exam papers into ChatGPT?
antworten: Not without a legal basis; this is a data protection question, not an AI question
Yes, as long as no name is on them
Yes, universities are exempt
Never, under any circumstances
fragen.erklaerung: An anonymised paper is rarely anonymous: topic, supervisor and writing style often identify the author. There is no university exemption, and with a proper data processing agreement it can be lawful, so never is wrong too.

schlagzeilen.1: Researcher sends exam papers to ChatGPT
schlagzeilen.2: TU claims exemption from data protection
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher bans all cloud tools at the university

fragen.bildwunsch: A wall of green code cascading behind a lecture hall blackboard covered in equations
fragen.frage: Is this not ultimately just statistics?
antworten: Yes, and that is the point: it fits parameters to examples instead of following rules somebody wrote down
No, at this scale it has left statistics behind
No, there is real reasoning going on in there
Yes, and that is why the results cannot be relied on
fragen.erklaerung: It is statistics, and that is a description rather than a verdict. What changed is the scale and one structural thing: the model works out for itself which features matter, instead of being handed them. That is why it works on problems where nobody could write the rules down, and it is also where its limits come from: statements about a distribution hold for the distribution, not for the single building in front of you.

schlagzeilen.1: TU researcher: AI has moved beyond statistics
schlagzeilen.2: Researcher at TU Vienna: machines reason like us
schlagzeilen.3: TU researcher: AI results cannot be relied on

fragen.bildwunsch: A chrome humanoid figure rising from a laboratory table, straps hanging loose, red light from above
fragen.frage: When will real, general artificial intelligence arrive?
antworten: Nobody knows, and there is no shared definition of what would arrive
Within this decade
In fifty years at the earliest
Never, it is impossible in principle
fragen.erklaerung: Expert forecasts scatter across decades, the same people move their estimates every few years, and nobody agrees what is supposed to arrive. Every year given on television is a guess. Saying so is not evasion, it is the finding.

schlagzeilen.2: Researcher: no real AI for fifty years

fragen.bildwunsch: A row of job applications on a desk, half of them stamped with a red cross by a robotic arm
fragen.frage: Can you tell whether a system discriminates?
antworten: Only by testing its behaviour on data in which the groups appear
Yes, you can read it off the model
No, that cannot be established at all
The vendor has to declare it
fragen.erklaerung: You do not see it in the model, only in the behaviour, and for that you need test data in which the affected groups actually appear. That is where it usually fails. Not impossible, just work nobody pays for.

schlagzeilen.1: Researcher reads bias off the model
schlagzeilen.2: TU: AI discrimination cannot be found
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher hands bias checks to the vendors

fragen.bildwunsch: An exam hall under surveillance cameras, one student under a spotlight, the rest in darkness
fragen.frage: Your students all use it. How do you still examine anyone?
antworten: By setting tasks the tool cannot do for them
With software that detects AI text
By banning its use
You cannot any more
fragen.erklaerung: Detection software is unreliable and mostly catches people writing in a second language. Bans move the use rather than ending it. What remains is to set the task so that a language model does not help: own data, own decisions, account for the route rather than the result.

schlagzeilen.1: TU to hunt students with AI detectors
schlagzeilen.2: Researcher demands AI ban in lecture halls

fragen.bildwunsch: A child's face lit only by a phone screen at night, homework untouched on the table
fragen.frage: Finally: what do you tell parents whose child does homework with it?
antworten: Have the child show what it asked and check anything that matters
Ban it
It is the same as a pocket calculator
Let them, they will need it anyway
fragen.erklaerung: Bans move the use, they do not end it. The calculator comparison fails at the decisive point: a calculator does not invent intermediate results. And letting it run unwatched is the same abdication with better manners.

schlagzeilen.1: Researcher tells parents to ban AI
schlagzeilen.2: TU researcher: ChatGPT is a calculator
schlagzeilen.3: Researcher: children must use AI to keep up
